name: @olai/server
//main: src/serve.ts, not src/main.ts: main.ts ends in a top-level run that starts the server and installs signal handlers, so a resolver honouring `main` over `exports` would boot a listener on import. The binary is reached as a script path (default.nix, the justfile), never as a module.
//dependencies: Runtime dependencies support generic host composition, transports, process shutdown and the application command-line client. The bundle owns the selected module catalogue, application surface and exposure maps. Plugin packages below are test-only contracts and fixtures.
//ws: Not here any more, and that is the point of serveSurfaceApp: no source in this package names a websocket implementation. `ws` is the hydrated @kolu/surface-app's own peer dependency, declared at the ROOT with the rest of them (bunfig.toml has the argument).
//devDependencies: @olai/child is the subprocess socket the process-boundary tests ride (`child.testlib.ts`, `surfaceCli.test.ts`); product spawn is `olai-plugin-chat`'s. `olai-plugin-git/testlib` is the repository builder `headless.test.ts` used to copy, and `olai-plugin-identity/who` is the gravatar hash `identity.test.ts` asserts a chip drew — one spelling of a URL rather than two, through a door with no Effect and no component in it; the fence carves those two the way it does for `@olai/tests`. Deliberately not a runtime dependency: nothing in the served binary imports it.
//: The process composition root and command-line entry. It supplies operator paths and generic host capabilities, then mounts the selected bundle. Domain surfaces and face policy belong to the bundle and its providers; the permanent host serves only management without them. No production source imports a plugin implementation. Browser assets arrive as a built directory, never as a dependency on the browser package.
